correctness.rationale: For the repaired cyclic orientation, B^T maps the vertex torus onto the stated edge torus with diagonal circle kernel, by summing the consecutive edge differences. Under signed reorientation B'=BS the torus, matrix and phase variables transform together: Z'=SZ, K'=SKS, and the sine map commutes with S. For h≤1/Λ the strict sine-secant inequality gives injectivity of the lift even at equality; lattice and rotation equivariance, compactness and degree one give a quotient homeomorphism. The lower bound on the quotient derivative is positive in the strict interval, and the boundary witnesses have a kernel (all π for even n; one zero for odd n, retaining a vector in the two-dimensional top eigenspace perpendicular to the exceptional edge). For h>1/Λ, balanced ±arccos(c) phases with c just below −1/(hΛ) obey closure, adding a zero edge for odd n. The even-cycle top eigenspace is simple, and in the odd case the exceptional edge's nonzero top Fourier projection removes one, but only one, of the two zero directions at the critical cosine. The remaining direction crosses to negative, with all others positive. On an inverse branch from this regular negative source, regular values of the full map form a nonempty open set by Sard and compactness. Degree +1 then gives at least two positive preimages in addition to the negative one.
residual_risks: The verifier was inspected, not executed. It samples Jacobian inertia and endpoint nullity, not the topological conclusion. The repaired proof asserts neither exact fibre cardinality nor dynamics of iterates.
